7	\subsection{Cross-Task Validation: Event Extraction}
8	\label{sec:wikievents}
9	
10	To test generality beyond RE, we apply OntoCoDec to event extraction (EE) on WikiEvents~\cite{li2021document} (56 event types, 80 argument roles, 27 entity types, 245 role$\to$type constraints; Appendix~\ref{app:wikievents}).
11	The constraint framework requires no architectural modification: the grammar layer compiles event/role vocabularies into a CFG; the semantic layer enforces role-conditioned entity type constraints via the same stateful registry mechanism.
12	The violation taxonomy extends naturally: Event Vocabulary (EV), Role Vocabulary (RoV), Argument Constraint (AC, analogous to DR), Entity Type (ET), and Cross-Field (CF).
13	
14	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
15	%  Table: WikiEvents three-model comparison (v3 final)
16	%  exp_ids: ee_{qwen,llama,mistral}_wikievents_{unconstrained,grammar_only,constrained_v3}
17	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
18	\begin{table}[t]
19	\centering
20	\small
21	\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2.8pt}
22	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
23	\begin{tabular}{@{}ll rrrr rr@{}}

25	& & \multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{Violation Rates (\%)}}
26	& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\

55	\paragraph{Results.}
56	Unconstrained generation produces extreme vocabulary violations (EV+RoV exceeding 85\% combined; Table~\ref{tab:wikievents}), and all models yield entity F1\,=\,0 because the parser cannot identify well-formed mentions in off-schema output.
57	Full S1 eliminates EV and RoV across all three models ($\to$\,0\%), validating tokenizer-agnostic design across byte-level BPE (Qwen, Llama) and SentencePiece (Mistral).
58	Grammar-only ablation isolates each layer: grammar eliminates EV ($\to$\,0\%) but leaves RoV at 64--77\% because the CFG cannot constrain 80 argument roles conditioned on event context; AC rises from near-zero to 8--14\%, replicating the latent-violation surfacing pattern from DocRED (\S\ref{sec:docred-results}).
59	Full S1 then drives RoV to 0\%, confirming layer complementarity.
60	Residual AC (1.3--3.8\%) traces to confusion between semantically similar entity types (e.g., SID vs.\ SEN) where grammar-first fallback permits the incorrect type; CF rises to 15--21\%, consistent with the per-slot enforcement trade-off in RE.
61	
62	Post-hoc filtering is impractical for EE: it retains only 23/5{,}467 arguments for Qwen (99.6\% discarded), 3/5{,}053 for Llama, and 0/6{,}034 for Mistral, because unconstrained models generate generic role names rather than ontology-specific ones.
63	Unlike RE, where constraints are F1-neutral, EE shows measurable gains: entity F1 rises from 0\% to 11.7--17.6\% and trigger F1 increases by $+$1.5--1.8\,pp, because grammar enforcement produces schema-valid JSON that the parser can process.
64

75	%  (a) Core result
76	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
77	\paragraph{Core result: DR elimination at zero F1 cost.}
78	The full two-layer constraint configuration (S1) reduces domain/range
79	violations from 15.37\% to 0.93\%, a 94\% relative reduction,
80	% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
81	while relation F1 moves from 8.23 to 8.36 ($+$0.13\,pp; bootstrap 95\% CI [$-$0.24, $+$0.58]\,pp, $p = 0.58$, 10{,}000 iterations).
82	% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836
83	% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824
84	The difference is not statistically significant ($p = 0.58$), confirming
85	that constraint enforcement is F1-neutral on this dataset.
86	Post-hoc filtering achieves higher F1 in most zero-shot settings via precision gains from aggressive violation removal (SciERC: 8.63 vs.\ 8.36; DocRED: 9.61 vs.\ 8.23), but at the cost of discarding up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (Appendix~\ref{app:posthoc-extended}); OntoCoDec preserves recall by enforcing constraints during generation.
87	At the per-relation level, violations drop from 42.42\% to 2.82\% on
88	\textsc{Compare}, from 33.54\% to 1.21\% on \textsc{Feature-of}, and
89	reach 0\% on four of seven relation types
90	(\textsc{Conjunction}, \textsc{Hyponym-of}, \textsc{Part-of},
91	\textsc{Used-for}).
92	% phase2_scierc_full_s1 per_relation_dr: Compare=0.0282,
93	%   Feature-of=0.0121, Hyponym-of=0, Part-of=0, Used-for=0, Conjunction=0
94	However, full constraint enforcement elevates cross-field consistency
95	violations from 0.08\% to 9.90\%;
96	% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: CF=0.0008; phase2_scierc_full_s1: CF=0.099
97	we analyze this trade-off in Section~\ref{sec:discussion}.
98	
99	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
100	%  (b) Grammar layer
101	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
102	\paragraph{Grammar layer: cost-free structural guarantees.}
103	Grammar-only constraints eliminate RV (1.39\%\,$\to$\,0\%) and ET (0.40\%\,$\to$\,0\%) with no F1 impact, while DR remains unchanged (15.37\%\,$\to$\,14.84\%).
104	This configuration represents the capability ceiling of grammar-based constrained decoding~\cite{geng2023gcd}, which enforces JSON structure and vocabulary membership but cannot reason about cross-field semantic constraints.
105	% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823
106	
107	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
108	%  (c) Enabling dependency
109	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
110	\paragraph{Enabling dependency.}
111	Semantic-only constraints reduce DR by only 24\% (15.37\%\,$\to$\,11.65\%) and cannot eliminate RV (1.51\%) or ET (0.40\%).
112	% phase2_scierc_semantic_only: DR=0.1165, RV=0.0151, ET=0.004
113	The residual ET under semantic-only arises because the semantic mask constrains type tokens to relation-specific valid sets but cannot enforce vocabulary membership; occasionally the mask excludes the model's preferred valid-vocabulary type, forcing an OOV alternative.
114	Under full mode, the grammar layer's intersection prevents this, confirming the \emph{enabling dependency}: without grammar-enforced vocabulary, the semantic layer encounters OOV relation types with no domain/range rules.
115	Adding the grammar layer yields a further 92\% relative reduction (11.65\%\,$\to$\,0.93\%).
116	% phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093
117	
118	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
119	%  (d) S1 vs S2
120	% ──────────────────────────────────────────
121	\paragraph{S1 vs.\ S2.}
122	S2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\%) but lower R-F1 (8.03 vs.\ 8.36) with fewer triples (1{,}644 vs.\ 1{,}729) and does not resolve the CF trade-off (8.03\% vs.\ 9.90\%); we adopt S1 as the primary configuration.
123	% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644

129	\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
130	\label{sec:composability}
131	Table~\ref{tab:composability} presents the composability matrix on SciERC for both Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B (zero-shot vs.\ LoRA fine-tuned $\times$ unconstrained vs.\ full S1), testing whether OntoCoDec composes with task-specific fine-tuning across model families.
132	% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_full_s1,
133	%          w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,
134	%          llama_scierc_unconstrained, llama_scierc_full_s1,
135	%          w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval
136	
137	Fine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\% but leaves residual violations on tight-constraint relations (Table~\ref{tab:composability}).
138	Adding S1 eliminates these: Qwen DR 1.95\%\,$\to$\,0\% ($-$0.09\,pp R-F1), Llama DR 1.11\%\,$\to$\,0.09\% ($+$0.02\,pp).
139	On DocRED, the same pattern holds: Qwen DR 0.76\%\,$\to$\,0.01\% ($-$0.30\,pp), Llama DR 0.49\%\,$\to$\,0.20\% ($+$0.51\,pp).
140	% w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.01%, R-F1=40.56; w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.20%, R-F1=44.23
141	
142	Across all settings, fine-tuned + S1 yields DR\,$\leq$\,0.20\% with R-F1 within $\pm$0.6\,pp, confirming orthogonal composability.
143	The four-way ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:ft-ablation}) shows grammar is a no-op post-fine-tuning; the semantic layer alone reduces DR by 39--72\%.
144	CF interference drops from $+$9.82\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\,pp (fine-tuned) for Qwen, tracing to \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X schema ambiguity rather than enforcement failure (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}).
145	Beam search ($k{=}4$) offers an orthogonal path: on SciERC, it eliminates residual DR entirely and reduces CF from 9.90\% to 0.53\% for Qwen, and from 6.56\% to 0.93\% for Llama (Appendix~\ref{app:beam-search}).

      "content": "% Section 5 — SciERC Results (Draft)\n% Data source: Phase 2 SciERC registry experiments\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_grammar_only,\n% & 8.03\n  & 8.03  & \\textbf{31.90} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}}%\n\\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 documents, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).\nDR: domain/range violation rate;\nRV: relation vocabulary violation rate;\nET: entity type violation rate;\nCF: cross-field consistency violation rate.\n$\\Delta$DR: relative DR reduction vs.\\ the unconstrained baseline.\n$\\downarrow$\\,/\\,$\\uparrow$: lower\\,/\\,higher is better.\nBest per column in \\textbf{bold} (CF excluded; see text).\nF1 scores are multiplied by 100.\nStatistical significance assessed via bootstrap resampling (10{,}000 iterations).}\n\\label{tab:scierc-ablation}\n\\end{table}\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (a) Core result\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Core result: DR elimination at zero F1 cost.}\nThe full two-layer constraint configuration (S1) reduces domain/range\nviolations from 15.37\\% to 0.93\\%, a 94\\% relative reduction,\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093\nwhile relation F1 moves from 8.23 to 8.36 ($+$0.13\\,pp; bootstrap 95\\% CI [$-$0.24, $+$0.58]\\,pp, $p = 0.58$, 10{,}000 iterations).\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836\n% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824\nThe difference is not statistically significant ($p = 0.58$), confirming\nthat constraint enforcement is F1-neutral on this dataset.\nPost-hoc filtering achieves higher F1 in most zero-shot settings via precision gains from aggressive violation removal (SciERC: 8.63 vs.\\ 8.36; DocRED: 9.61 vs.\\ 8.23), but at the cost of discarding up to 48\\% of predictions including true positives (Appendix~\\ref{app:posthoc-extended}); OntoCoDec preserves recall by enforcing constraints during generation.\nAt the per-relation level, violations drop from 42.42\\% to 2.82\\% on\n\\textsc{Compare}, from 33.54\\% to 1.21\\% on \\textsc{Feature-of}, and\nreach 0\\% on four of seven relation types\n(\\textsc{Conjunction}, \\textsc{Hyponym-of}, \\textsc{Part-of},\n\\textsc{Used-for}).\n% phase2_scierc_full_s1 per_relation_dr: Compare=0.0282,\n%   Feature-of=0.0121, Hyponym-of=0, Part-of=0, Used-for=0, Conjunction=0\nHowever, full constraint enforcement elevates cross-field consistency\nviolations from 0.08\\% to 9.90\\%;\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: CF=0.0008; phase2_scierc_full_s1: CF=0.099\nwe analyze this trade-off in Section~\\ref{sec:discussion}.\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (b) Grammar layer\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Grammar layer: cost-free structural guarantees.}\nGrammar-only constraints eliminate RV (1.39\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\%) and ET (0.40\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\%) with no F1 impact, while DR remains unchanged (15.37\\%\\,$\\to$\\,14.84\\%).\nThis configuration represents the capability ceiling of grammar-based constrained decoding~\\cite{geng2023gcd}, which enforces JSON structure and vocabulary membership but cannot reason about cross-field semantic constraints.\n% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (c) Enabling dependency\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Enabling dependency.}\nSemantic-only constraints reduce DR by only 24\\% (15.37\\%\\,$\\to$\\,11.65\\%) and cannot eliminate RV (1.51\\%) or ET (0.40\\%).\n% phase2_scierc_semantic_only: DR=0.1165, RV=0.0151, ET=0.004\nThe residual ET under semantic-only arises because the semantic mask constrains type tokens to relation-specific valid sets but cannot enforce vocabulary membership; occasionally the mask excludes the model's preferred valid-vocabulary type, forcing an OOV alternative.\nUnder full mode, the grammar layer's intersection prevents this, confirming the \\emph{enabling dependency}: without grammar-enforced vocabulary, the semantic layer encounters OOV relation types with no domain/range rules.\nAdding the grammar layer yields a further 92\\% relative reduction (11.65\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.93\\%).\n% phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (d) S1 vs S2\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{S1 vs.\\ S2.}\nS2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\\%) but lower R-F1 (8.03 vs.\\ 8.36) with fewer triples (1{,}644 vs.\\ 1{,}729) and does not resolve the CF trade-off (8.03\\% vs.\\ 9.90\\%); we adopt S1 as the primary configuration.\n% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning\n%  exp_ids: lora_scierc_unconstrained, lora_scierc_full_s1\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}\n\\label{sec:composability}\nTable~\\ref{tab:composability} presents the composability matrix on SciERC for both Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B (zero-shot vs.\\ LoRA fine-tuned $\\times$ unconstrained vs.\\ full S1), testing whether OntoCoDec composes with task-specific fine-tuning across model families.\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_full_s1,\n%          w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,\n%          llama_scierc_unconstrained, llama_scierc_full_s1,\n%          w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval\n\nFine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\\% but leaves residual violations on tight-constraint relations (Table~\\ref{tab:composability}).\nAdding S1 eliminates these: Qwen DR 1.95\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\% ($-$0.09\\,pp R-F1), Llama DR 1.11\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.09\\% ($+$0.02\\,pp).\nOn DocRED, the same pattern holds: Qwen DR 0.76\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.01\\% ($-$0.30\\,pp), Llama DR 0.49\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.20\\% ($+$0.51\\,pp).\n% w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.01%, R-F1=40.56; w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.20%, R-F1=44.23\n\nAcross all settings, fine-tuned + S1 yields DR\\,$\\leq$\\,0.20\\% with R-F1 within $\\pm$0.6\\,pp, confirming orthogonal composability.\nThe four-way ablation (Appendix~\\ref{app:ft-ablation}) shows grammar is a no-op post-fine-tuning; the semantic layer alone reduces DR by 39--72\\%.\nCF interference drops from $+$9.82\\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\\,pp (fine-tuned) for Qwen, tracing to \\textsc{Generic}$\\leftrightarrow$X schema ambiguity rather than enforcement failure (Appendix~\\ref{app:cf-distribution}).\nBeam search ($k{=}4$) offers an orthogonal path: on SciERC, it eliminates residual DR entirely and reduces CF from 9.90\\% to 0.53\\% for Qwen, and from 6.56\\% to 0.93\\% for Llama (Appendix~\\ref{app:beam-search}).\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3pt}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrrr experiments use Qwen3-8B in a zero-shot setting on 551 test documents\nwith identical prompts and decoding parameters;\nonly the active constraint layers differ.\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3.6pt}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrrr rr@{}}\n\\toprule\n& RV\\,$\\downarrow$ & ET\\,$\\downarrow$ & CF\n  & Rel.\\,$\\uparrow$ & Ent.\\,$\\uparrow$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nUnconstrained\n  & 15.37 & ---\n  & 1.39  & 0.40\n  & 0.08\n  & 8.23  & 31.01 \\\\\nGrammar\n  & 14.84 & $\\downarrow$3\\%\n  & \\textbf{0} & \\textbf{0}\n  & 0.08\n  & 8.23  & 30.98 \\\\\nSemantic\n  & 11.65 & $\\downarrow$24\\%\n  & 1.51  & 0.40\n  & 2.71\n  & 8.15  & 31.01 \\\\\nFull (S1)\n  & \\textbf{0.93} & $\\downarrow$\\textbf{94\\%}\n  & \\textbf{0} & \\textbf{0}\n  & 9.90\n  & \\textbf{8.36} & 30.98 \\\\\nFull (S2)\n  & 0.97  & $\\downarrow$94\\%\n  & \\textbf{0} & \\textbf{0}\n  & 8.03\n  & 8.03  & \\textbf{31.90} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}}%\n\\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 documents, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).\nDR: domain/range violation rate;\nRV: relation vocabulary violation rate;\nET: entity type violation rate;\nCF: cross-field consistency violation rate.\n$\\Delta$DR: relative DR reduction vs.\\ the unconstrained baseline.\n$\\downarrow$\\,/\\,$\\uparrow$: lower\\,/\\,higher is better.\nBest per column in \\textbf{bold} (CF excluded; see text).\nF1 scores are multiplied by 100.\nStatistical significance assessed via bootstrap resampling (10{,}000 iterations).}\n\\label{tab:scierc-ablation}\n\\end{table}\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (a) Core result\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Core result: DR elimination at zero F1 cost.}\nThe full two-layer constraint configuration (S1) reduces domain/range\nviolations from 15.37\\% to 0.93\\%, a 94\\% relative reduction,\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093\nwhile relation F1 moves from 8.23 to 8.36 ($+$0.13\\,pp; bootstrap 95\\% CI [$-$0.24, $+$0.58]\\,pp, $p = 0.58$, 10{,}000 iterations).\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836\n% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824\nThe difference is not statistically significant ($p = 0.58$), confirming\nthat constraint enforcement is F1-neutral on this dataset.\nPost-hoc filtering achieves higher F1 in most zero-shot settings via precision gains from aggressive violation removal (SciERC: 8.63 vs.\\ 8.36; DocRED: 9.61 vs.\\ 8.23), but at the cost of discarding up to 48\\% of predictions including true positives (Appendix~\\ref{app:posthoc-extended}); OntoCoDec preserves recall by enforcing constraints during generation.\nAt the per-relation level, violations drop from 42.42\\% to 2.82\\% on\n\\textsc{Compare}, from 33.54\\% to 1.21\\% on \\textsc{Feature-of}, and\nreach 0\\% on four of seven relation types\n(\\textsc{Conjunction}, \\textsc{Hyponym-of}, \\textsc{Part-of},\n\\textsc{Used-for}).\n% phase2_scierc_full_s1 per_relation_dr: Compare=0.0282,\n%   Feature-of=0.0121, Hyponym-of=0, Part-of=0, Used-for=0, Conjunction=0\nHowever, full constraint enforcement elevates cross-field consistency\nviolations from 0.08\\% to 9.90\\%;\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: CF=0.0008; phase2_scierc_full_s1: CF=0.099\nwe analyze this trade-off in Section~\\ref{sec:discussion}.\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (b) Grammar layer\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Grammar layer: cost-free structural guarantees.}\nGrammar-only constraints eliminate RV (1.39\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\%) and ET (0.40\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\%) with no F1 impact, while DR remains unchanged (15.37\\%\\,$\\to$\\,14.84\\%).\nThis configuration represents the capability ceiling of grammar-based constrained decoding~\\cite{geng2023gcd}, which enforces JSON structure and vocabulary membership but cannot reason about cross-field semantic constraints.\n% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (c) Enabling dependency\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Enabling dependency.}\nSemantic-only constraints reduce DR by only 24\\% (15.37\\%\\,$\\to$\\,11.65\\%) and cannot eliminate RV (1.51\\%) or ET (0.40\\%).\n% phase2_scierc_semantic_only: DR=0.1165, RV=0.0151, ET=0.004\nThe residual ET under semantic-only arises because the semantic mask constrains type tokens to relation-specific valid sets but cannot enforce vocabulary membership; occasionally the mask excludes the model's preferred valid-vocabulary type, forcing an OOV alternative.\nUnder full mode, the grammar layer's intersection prevents this, confirming the \\emph{enabling dependency}: without grammar-enforced vocabulary, the semantic layer encounters OOV relation types with no domain/range rules.\nAdding the grammar layer yields a further 92\\% relative reduction (11.65\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.93\\%).\n% phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (d) S1 vs S2\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{S1 vs.\\ S2.}\nS2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\\%) but lower R-F1 (8.03 vs.\\ 8.36) with fewer triples (1{,}644 vs.\\ 1{,}729) and does not resolve the CF trade-off (8.03\\% vs.\\ 9.90\\%); we adopt S1 as the primary configuration.\n% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning\n%  exp_ids: lora_scierc_unconstrained, lora_scierc_full_s1\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}\n\\label{sec:composability}\nTable~\\ref{tab:composability} presents the composability matrix on SciERC for both Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B (zero-shot vs.\\ LoRA fine-tuned $\\times$ unconstrained vs.\\ full S1), testing whether OntoCoDec composes with task-specific fine-tuning across model families.\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_full_s1,\n%          w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,\n%          llama_scierc_unconstrained, llama_scierc_full_s1,\n%          w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval\n\nFine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\\% but leaves residual violations on tight-constraint relations (Table~\\ref{tab:composability}).\nAdding S1 eliminates these: Qwen DR 1.95\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\% ($-$0.09\\,pp R-F1), Llama DR 1.11\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.09\\% ($+$0.02\\,pp).\nOn DocRED, the same pattern holds: Qwen DR 0.76\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.01\\% ($-$0.30\\,pp), Llama DR 0.49\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.20\\% ($+$0.51\\,pp).\n% w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.01%, R-F1=40.56; w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.20%, R-F1=44.23\n\nAcross all settings, fine-tuned + S1 yields DR\\,$\\leq$\\,0.20\\% with R-F1 within $\\pm$0.6\\,pp, confirming orthogonal composability.\nThe four-way ablation (Appendix~\\ref{app:ft-ablation}) shows grammar is a no-op post-fine-tuning; the semantic layer alone reduces DR by 39--72\\%.\nCF interference drops from $+$9.82\\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\\,pp (fine-tuned) for Qwen, tracing to \\textsc{Generic}$\\leftrightarrow$X schema ambiguity rather than enforcement failure (Appendix~\\ref{app:cf-distribution}).\nBeam search ($k{=}4$) offers an orthogonal path: on SciERC, it eliminates residual DR entirely and reduces CF from 9.90\\% to 0.53\\% for Qwen, and from 6.56\\% to 0.93\\% for Llama (Appendix~\\ref{app:beam-search}).\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3pt}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrrr & 30.98 & $\\downarrow$94\\% \\\\\n\\cmidrule(l){2-8}\n  & \\multirow{2}{*}{LoRA}\n    & Unconstr.\\ &  1.95 & 0    & 43.86 & 67.05 & --- \\\\\n  & & Full S1    & \\textbf{0} & 1.18 & 43.77 & 67.05 & Discussion and Conclusion

OntoCoDec compiles IE ontology schemas into
composable token-level decoding constraints,
achieving 42–99% DR reduction across three models and three datasets (2 RE + 1 EE) with no significant RE F1 cost; in EE, format compliance additionally enables entity extraction (§5.5). Composed
with LoRA fine-tuning, DR reaches ≤ 0.20% at
<0.6 pp F1 cost; residual DR follows a dual-factor
pattern (κ̄ × RVbaseline ; Appendix C). CF impact is
model-dependent (up to 12% for calibrated models,
reduced for poorly-calibrated ones); fine-tuning resolves this tension (CF ≤ 1.2%; §5.2), and beam
search (k=4) eliminates both residual DR and CF

Runtime overhead. Full S1 adds +2.3% on SciERC and +5.4% on DocRED (same GPU); under
fine-tuning, overhead drops to +2.3% (61 ms/doc).
Grammar compile is a one-time 44 ms cost. Perlayer profiling in Appendix C.

60	\paragraph{Core result.}
61	Full S1 reduces DR from 18.46\% to 10.21\% ($\downarrow$45\%), eliminates ET (2.48\%\,$\to$\,0\%), and near-eliminates RV (29.66\%\,$\to$\,0.03\%; residual traces to tokenization edge cases where multi-token relation names span grammar-state boundaries).
62	Relation F1 improves from 7.74 to 8.23 ($+$0.50\,pp; bootstrap 95\% CI [$+$0.23, $+$0.81], $p < 0.001$), attributable to grammar-layer elimination of 5{,}189 OOV relation predictions counted as false positives.
63	CF increases modestly (0.10\%\,$\to$\,2.57\%), lower than SciERC's 9.90\%, consistent with the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off analyzed in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.
64	
65	% exp_ids: phase2_docred_grammar_only
66	\paragraph{Grammar layer surfaces latent violations.}
67	Grammar-only constraints eliminate RV and ET but \emph{increase} DR to 26.17\% ($+$42\%): the baseline's 29.66\% OOV triples cannot be evaluated for DR; grammar enforcement assigns valid relation names whose domain/range rules the associated types frequently violate, \emph{revealing} latent incompatibilities that motivate the semantic layer.
68	
69	% exp_ids: phase2_docred_semantic_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
70	\paragraph{Enabling dependency and tightness ceiling.}
71	Semantic-only reduces DR by 25\% but cannot eliminate RV (29.87\%) or prevent ET increases (2.48\%\,$\to$\,4.22\%), replicating SciERC's enabling dependency.
72	Residual DR (10.21\%) exceeds SciERC's (0.93\%) due to higher constraint tightness ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$ vs.\ 0.333), with fallback rate (10.2\%) closely tracking residual DR (Appendix~\ref{app:fallback-coverage}).

1	% Section: Constraint Composition (compressed, 787→~500 words)
2	
3	At each decoding step $t$, let $G(t) \subseteq V$ and $S(t) \subseteq V$ denote the tokens permitted by the grammar and semantic layers, respectively.
4	The final mask is their conjunction:
5	%
6	\begin{equation}\label{eq:composition}
7	  M_{\text{final}}(t) = M_{\text{grammar}}(t) \;\wedge\; M_{\text{semantic}}(t),
8	\end{equation}
9	%
10	so a token is allowed only if it satisfies \emph{both} structural and type-level constraints.
11	The conjunction is asymmetric: $S(t)$ is defined only over $G(t)$, reflecting the enabling dependency (\S\ref{sec:method}): the semantic layer requires the relation type to belong to $\mathcal{R}$, a property guaranteed only by the grammar layer.
12	
13	\paragraph{Grammar-First Fallback.}
14	When $S(t) \cap G(t) = \emptyset$ (tight constraints leave no token that is both grammar-valid and semantically valid), na\"{\i}ve masking would force selection of a grammar-invalid token, breaking JSON structure.
15	We enforce a \emph{grammar-first fallback}: if no semantically valid token survives grammar filtering, semantic masking is skipped and the grammar layer alone controls selection.
16	Structural integrity is a hard constraint; a type violation is a soft error detectable by downstream validation.
17	
18	\paragraph{Constraint Tightness.}
19	We define the tightness of relation $r$ as:
20	%
21	\begin{equation}\label{eq:tightness}
22	  \kappa(r) = 1 - \frac{|\mathcal{V}(r)|}{|\mathcal{E}|^2},
23	\end{equation}
24	%
25	where $\mathcal{V}(r)$ is the set of valid type pairs and $\mathcal{E}$ the entity type vocabulary.
26	The mean tightness $\bar{\kappa} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}|}\sum_{r} \kappa(r)$ characterizes ontology restrictiveness.
27	Tighter constraints eliminate more grammar-valid tokens at type-bearing positions, increasing fallback frequency and residual DR.
28	This dual-factor pattern (tightness $\times$ baseline model violation rate) is consistent with the cross-dataset results: for calibrated models (Qwen, Llama), SciERC ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.333$, 24 valid pairs/relation) achieves 94--99\% DR reduction, while DocRED ($\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$, 5.68 pairs) achieves 45--90\%; including Mistral (whose high baseline ET shifts the regime), the full range across all three models is 42--99\% (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}; quantitative analysis in Appendix~\ref{app:dual-factor}).
29	
30	\paragraph{Non-Rectangularity and Sequential Masking.}
31	\label{sec:rectangularity}
32	% Data source: artifacts/rebuttal/w2_rectangularity_report.md
33	The sequential masking strategy ($\tau^h \in \operatorname{dom}(r)$, then $\tau^t \in \operatorname{range}(r, \tau^h)$) is necessary because real ontology type signatures are overwhelmingly non-rectangular: 0/7 SciERC and only 23/96 DocRED relations satisfy $\sigma(r) = \operatorname{dom}(r) \times \operatorname{range}(r)$.
34	Independent enforcement ($\tau^h \in \operatorname{dom}(r) \wedge \tau^t \in \operatorname{range}(r)$) would admit 33.3\% (SciERC) and 36.8\% (DocRED) spurious type pairs. On SciERC, 100\% of residual DR violations under full S1 are pairs that pass independent checks but violate $\sigma(r)$.
35	OntoCoDec's sequential approach achieves exact pair-based enforcement without explicit enumeration of $\sigma(r)$ at each step, exploiting the autoregressive left-to-right generation order.
36	
37	\paragraph{Decidability Taxonomy.}
38	We classify constraints by when sufficient information becomes available: \emph{local} (current token only, e.g., vocabulary membership; grammar layer), \emph{prefix-decidable} (decoded prefix, e.g., domain/range; semantic layer), and \emph{non-local} (forward coreference; outside single-pass decoding, partially addressed by S2, \S\ref{sec:s2}).
39
